name: The Room That Remembers You Wrong
premise:
A familiar room labels every object with a different version of your life. One
photo calls you by the wrong name. One coat remembers a job you never had. The
room is trying to settle on a history.

objective.description: Leave without letting the room overwrite a personal anchor.

anchors.name: true_name
anchors.description: Your own name, spoken in your own voice.

anchors.name: first_home
anchors.description: The first room you remember calling yours.

labels.observe_text:
The object labels conflict. Masking them will stop new false histories from
being read while you reclaim the correct anchor.

name_anchor.observe_text:
Your true name is the cleanest anchor in the room. Reclaim it before the
room chooses a replacement.

personal_history.observe_text:
You could rewrite yourself to fit the room. That would end the argument by
losing it.

doorway.observe_text:
The door is open, but leaving without masking the labels lets the room keep
writing after you.

reclaim.scene_message: You speak your true name until the room has to spell it correctly.
reclaim.system_note: Anchor reclaimed. A mask is still needed to stop further overwrite.
reclaim.discovered_rule: Some objectives protect anchors rather than repairing scenery.

temporary.scene_message: The false labels blur into harmless static. They can no longer overwrite you.

match_room.scene_message: The room becomes comfortable by making you less certain who entered it.
match_room.system_note: Self-history rewrite. It does not reclaim the correct anchor.

soften.scene_message: The doorway feels easier to cross. The room keeps writing labels behind you.

room_memory.text:
The room is attacking identity through records. Reclaim the correct anchor,
then mask the labels so they stop writing alternatives.

scene_progression.message: The labels settle. One wrong biography becomes easier to remember than your own.

hidden_rules: Some levels require protection and sequencing, not one visible repair.
Rewriting self history to match a broken environment is a loss.
